title: Heterogeneous session tail-latency harness: measure p95 & tokens/sec under dynamic micro-batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible load-testing harness that exercises dynamic micro-batching + session-aware queueing with mixed client profiles and measures end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) and tail latencies (p95/p99). Motivation: existing harnesses focus on steady-state arrival patterns; production traffic is heterogeneous (short chat turns, long single-shot completions, background embedding jobs) and exhibits transient bursts. We need to quantify how micro-batching and queueing policies amplify tail latency for different mixes and to add automated regression detection for operator rollouts.

Scope and success criteria:
- Implement traffic generator that models 4 session classes: conversational short-turn (mean 8 tokens), interactive medium (mean 48 tokens), long completion (mean 512 tokens), and embeddings (fixed 1536 tokens). Mixes will be parameterizable (e.g., 60/30/8/2 and stress mixes with 40/40/15/5).
- Integrate with runtime to measure per-request KPIs: tokens_in, tokens_out, request_enqueue_time, dequeue_time, start_decode_time, end_time. Export metrics to Prometheus and record histograms for p50/p90/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec aggregated by model and route.
- Add a canary scoring function that computes weighted SLO violation rate and a regression delta vs baseline; alert on >8% relative increase in p95 or >12% tokens/sec reduction.
- Reproduce three experiment templates: steady-state low-load, bursty arrival (Pareto/Poisson mix), and ramp-to-saturation with autoscaling off.

Methodology highlights:
- Traffic generator will implement session stickiness: new requests from same session reuse KV cache state to exercise prefix-cache benefits and to reveal p95 amplification from cache-miss churn.
- Micro-batcher simulated: allow variable batch-sizing harvest windows (1ms..20ms) and token-limited batching. Measure queue length distribution and queueing delay component separately from CPU/GPU decode time.
- Use noise injection to simulate GC/compaction pauses in the host process to observe interaction with batching windows.

Metrics and artifacts to produce:
- Artifacts: benchmark harness code (GitHub link), experiment configs (YAML), raw traces (ndjson), aggregated dashboards (Grafana links), and a reproducible experiment notebook (Colab/Notebooks).
- Primary metrics: overall tokens/sec, p95 end-to-end latency, queueing_delay_p95, decode_time_p95, batch_size_distribution percentiles, cache_hit_rate by session class, SLO_violation_fraction.

Outcomes expected:
- Quantitative sensitivity curves: p95 vs offered load for each mix and batching window, tokens/sec vs batching window, and queueing amplification heatmaps.
- Recommendations for default micro-batching window and policy per customer tier, and canary thresholds for rollout automation.

Implementation plan:
1) Week 1: implement multi-class traffic generator, session stickiness, and basic telemetry hooks (Aisha + Miguel).
2) Week 2: integrate micro-batcher config knobs into runtime test harness, export Prometheus metrics and add experiment templates (Miguel).
3) Week 3: run baseline matrix, add canary scoring logic and CI job that runs a reduced experiment for every runtime PR (integration with CI) (Aisha).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: experiments sensitive to infra noise. Mitigation: run 5 seeds and report median + MAD, control for background cluster activity, and single-tenant dedicated nodes for final runs.
- Risk: large trace volume. Mitigation: sample detailed traces (1%) and aggregate histograms for the rest.
